chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about the seminal fluid (al-madhy), so he said: 'It does not break the wudu (ablution), and one does not have to wash the clothes or the body from it; rather, it is at the status of mucus and saliva.'

key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: Pre-seminal fluid, a thin clear fluid released during arousal
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: Minor ablution, ritual washing for prayer

ai.seo_question: Does pre-seminal fluid (madhy) break wudu or require washing clothes?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (or al-Baqir) clarifies the fiqh of *al-madhy* (pre-seminal fluid) by distinguishing it from *al-manī* (seminal fluid). The Imam likens its purity status to mucus and saliva, establishing that it does not break *wudu* nor require washing the body or garments, a ruling that simplifies ritual purity for daily worship. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for differentiating between minor impurities that require wiping and major impurities requiring full washing.
